summary: Steel tower dated to 2013 by Alberta's register; the Ansell locality began as a 1911 railway siding, and the tower is listed active.

access.note: Register lists the tower as active, with access coded drive and a weather station. No source describes public visits.

events.note: Register year of construction for the present steel tower.

evidence.supports: Ansell record: steel tower, built 2013, 30 m tall, elevation 967.7 m
Ansell record: active, access coded drive
Ansell record: has a weather station
Ansell locality began in 1911 as a Grand Trunk Pacific railway siding serving coal mining along the Alberta Coal Branch
evidence.quote: established as a railway siding in 1911 by the Grand Trunk Pacific Railway

evidence.supports: the siding was founded to serve coal mining and transport on the Alberta Coal Branch
evidence.quote: was founded to serve coal mining and transportation activities along the Alberta Coal Branch railway line

evidence.supports: the site contains a fire and bear lookout tower, Ansell Tower
evidence.quote: The site contains a fire and bear lookout tower

evidence.supports: tower operated by the provincial government
Ansell is filed under the Edson Forest
each lookout site is staffed by a lookout observer, generally April to October
evidence.quote: Each site is staffed by a lookout observer whose job is to watch for wildfire all day, each day, generally from April to October.

sources.title: Wildfire Lookouts of Alberta (WF_WILDFIRE_LOOKOUT), FIRES database extract

notes_for_editor: Brief's access 'closed' is not stated by any source. The register codes Ansell as active with access 'drive', so it is recorded as restricted with no visit information. The history is thin: the register gives the 2013 build, and Wikipedia gives the locality history and the present-tense description of the tower. No source found gives the tower's own build reason or any fire record. Canada Lookouts has only the name and the Edson Forest line. Wikipedia's citation for the locality history is an Alberta Geographical Names entry, which the Wikipedia page cites rather than this story reading it directly. The brief has no local_unit, so the story says Alberta only.
